projects.name: Applause Meter
projects.description:
The Applause Meter is an embedded audio-sensing system that captures environmental sound and analyzes signal intensity to estimate audience engagement in real time. The project combines microphone-based sensing, signal processing, and threshold-based classification to distinguish applause from ambient background noise.

Designed as an applied engineering solution, the system converts raw acoustic input into a measurable response metric through a practical sensing and analysis pipeline. This project demonstrates hands-on experience with embedded electronics, real-time data interpretation, and designing reliable human-interaction systems.

projects.name: Maze Solver
projects.description:
A C maze-solving program that loads a maze from a text file, represents it in dynamically allocated memory, and searches for a valid route using recursive depth-first search. The solver marks explored paths, backtracks from dead ends, validates the completed solution, and cleans up its allocated memory.

projects.name: Sudoku Solver
projects.description:
A C Sudoku solver that parses a 9x9 puzzle from a text file and fills the board using recursive backtracking. Each candidate is checked against its row, column, and 3x3 zone before the solver advances or backtracks.
